authorityBoundary.siteIdentity: Unique normalized email plus bcrypt password; optional customer TOTP; opaque 30-day database-backed cookie session.
authorityBoundary.telegramIdentity: Telegram platform sender ID in bot and signed initData in Mini App/API; most initData consumers accept up to 24 hours and do not consume a nonce.
authorityBoundary.identityMerge: A logged-in site account may overwrite its telegram_id through a signed Telegram Login Widget callback; downstream history, swaps, wallets and CEX resolution use the merged Telegram ID.
authorityBoundary.adminIdentity: Separate Laravel password, immutable is_admin policy and mandatory encrypted TOTP with replay timestamp; it is not the customer account lifecycle.
authorityBoundary.nativeIdentity: No deployed native authentication, profile, account recovery or server-session handoff.
authorityBoundary.sessionStorage: Raw bearer and CSRF tokens are stored in web_sessions; expiry is enforced but there is no hash-at-rest, device inventory, rotation, revoke-all or security epoch.
authorityBoundary.recovery: No verified email ownership, forgot-password/reset, recovery-code, Telegram unlink/recovery, account deletion or formal support recovery workflow is deployed.
authorityBoundary.profileMoneyAuthority: The merged Telegram ID selects customer orders, swaps, wallet links, portfolio sources and referral state; this family does not itself sign funds but controls who can see and initiate adjacent customer workflows.

positiveControls: Passwords use bcrypt with per-hash salt; generic login failure does not distinguish unknown email from wrong password.
Session and CSRF tokens use cryptographic randomness; cookie is Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and path-bound.
Profile password, referral-address and TOTP mutations require an owner session plus CSRF; password change also checks the current password and TOTP disable checks the current factor.
Telegram assertions are HMAC verified and Mini App freshness has a strict shared future-skew check.
Database uniqueness prevents one email or Telegram identity from being linked to multiple web users concurrently.
Nginx applies explicit per-IP request limits to exact /login and /register routes.
Laravel operator auth has stronger encrypted TOTP and replay-timestamp semantics and is kept separate from customer identity.
criticalFindings: GET /auth/telegram/callback mutates the current account without CSRF/state, single-use nonce or fresh password/TOTP. A reusable signed Login Widget URL can overwrite an existing Telegram binding in a logged-in victim browser (login-CSRF/confused deputy), changing which Telegram-keyed orders, swaps, wallets, CEX sources and allowlist identity that victim site session resolves; it does not give the attacker the victim cookie directly.
Password change and TOTP enable/disable do not rotate or revoke any existing 30-day sessions; the password template explicitly tells the user that all sessions continue.

Customer TOTP secrets are stored as plaintext in web_users. Enrollment trusts a client-roundtripped hidden totp_secret and requires no fresh password/old-factor step-up; TOTP verification accepts a ±1 window and has no replay ledger.

The second-step login token is stateless and replayable for five minutes, uses a truncated 64-bit MAC, is coupled to INTERNAL_ADMIN_SECRET when configured, and accepts arbitrarily future timestamps because it checks only now minus timestamp greater than 300.

Raw 30-day session bearer tokens and CSRF tokens are database values. A database read becomes immediate session takeover; there is no session list, per-device metadata, rotation, revoke-all, password/2FA security epoch or inactivity bound.
Registration proves only email syntax, not ownership, and reveals whether an email exists. Password policy is only eight-character minimum; no reset/recovery lifecycle exists.
Logout is POST but performs no CSRF verification. SameSite=Lax is a useful browser mitigation, not an accepted application-level state-change authorization contract.

Nginx throttles only exact /login and /register. Password change, TOTP enable/disable and Telegram binding have no dedicated app/edge attempt limit; a stolen live session can make unbounded current-password or TOTP guesses.

Telegram Login Widget freshness only rejects assertions older than 24 hours and has no future-skew/lower-bound check, unlike the shared Mini App validator. A far-future timestamp still requires a valid Telegram signature, but clock/freshness drift fails open rather than closed.

Telegram identity, independent web-only negative IDs and Mini App initData form fragmented principals. There is no canonical merge/unmerge/recovery state machine or durable audit binding old identity, new identity, fresh authorization and session revocation.
Audit events log raw email or Telegram identifiers and lack a shared session/security-epoch correlation and explicit retention evidence.

telegramBot.reason: Telegram sender identity drives the customer profile and adjacent money workflows, but product-controlled session, revocation, MFA and recovery are absent.

site.reason: Registration, login/logout, profile, password, TOTP and Telegram binding are deployed with several positive controls, but identity merge, session lifecycle and recovery are unaccepted.

miniApp.reason: Signed Telegram initData is the primary customer authority for many APIs, generally reusable for up to 24 hours without nonce consumption; it is not the site session and inherits fragmented binding semantics.

admin.reason: Laravel has a stronger separate named-admin/TOTP contour and read-only WebUser model use, but customer-account recovery, privacy and operator support authority are not formally bounded.

api.reason: Cookie sessions, CSRF, Telegram widget/initData and repository mutations are directly exposed through mixed HTML/API routes without a versioned canonical subject/session/recovery contract.

native.reason: No native account/session/profile/recovery bridge exists; any future bridge must not turn server account recovery into native key recovery or signing authority.

limitations: Only public root/login GETs and service metadata were observed; no register/login/logout/profile/admin/API mutation or customer row was exercised.
Source shape proves deployed behavior and missing controls, not real-user lifecycle success, email ownership, Telegram account ownership or recovery outcomes.
Relay and bot checkout files differ from deployed production; all production claims are bound to exact deployed hashes.
No environment value, session/cookie, password hash, TOTP secret, customer identifier, database count or account record was read.

independentReviews.finding: Login-CSRF binding, long-lived non-revoked sessions, plaintext customer TOTP/session material and replayable second-step tokens prevent acceptance.
All six surfaces are classifiable, but identity authority is fragmented and recovery/unlink/native lifecycle is missing.
Positive bcrypt/cookie/CSRF/throttle controls support only a bounded source-verified classification, not production auth acceptance.
